title: Kanna Repo Config
description: `.kanna/config.json` is the shared repository contract. `.kanna/config.local.json` is read from the open checkout's working tree, never from the origin snapshot, and is deep-merged over the committed file with local values winning. Local config may contain only `agentProviders`, `workflow`, `ports`, `setup`, `teardown`, `test`, and `artifacts`; an unknown key, invalid JSON, or invalid value fails definition resolution and names the file. `agentProviders`, `ports`, and `artifacts` merge entry by entry, with a local entry replacing the committed entry of the same name. Every other permitted key replaces wholesale, and arrays never concatenate. Keep local config gitignored and do not put task-defining fields such as `vars`, `flavors`, `workspace`, `stage_order`, or reserved ports in it.

$schema.description: Set `$schema` to `https://schemas.kanna.build/config.schema.json` in every new `.kanna/config.json` and `.kanna/config.local.json`. Kanna publishes the schema with each merged version so editors and agents can discover supported fields and their semantics.

workflow.description: `workflow` selects the repository's default workflow by name. Kanna resolves a repo-authored `.kanna/workflows/<name>.json` before the bundled workflow of the same name. Workflow and agent definitions are public/listed by default; `visibility: internal` hides an effective definition from listings without preventing explicit resolution, and a repo override must redeclare it to remain internal. `flavors` selects a built-in variant by agent role (for example `"pr": "draft-pr"`); an explicit stage selector such as `pr@draft-pr` wins. Run `kanna-cli guide workflows` or call `kanna_guide {"topic":"workflows"}` before authoring a workflow.

setup.description: `setup`, `teardown`, and `test` are arrays of shell commands run from the repository or task worktree. `setup` prepares each new workspace before its agent starts. `teardown` runs best-effort when a task leaves a workspace. `test` records the repository's canonical verification commands for agents and workflows. Because local arrays replace rather than append, repeat every command that should remain when overriding one of these keys locally.

ports.description: `ports` maps environment-variable names to base ports; Kanna reserves task-specific ports and exports the resolved values so parallel worktrees do not collide. `vars` provides committed string substitutions for agent prompts. `workspace`, `stage_order`, `reserved_ports`, and `reserved_port_offsets` are committed task semantics and cannot appear in local config.

agentProviders.description: `agentProviders` maps exact agent names or `*` globs to a provider name or to `{ provider, model, effort }`; `provider` may be an ordered candidate list. Exact keys beat globs. Among matching globs, the most non-`*` characters wins and lexical order breaks ties. Selection precedence is: explicit task or stage override; matching `agentProviders` entry (including the local layer); layered `AGENT.md`/`EXTEND.md` frontmatter; global default provider. A rerun, resume, revision, or recovery reproduces the recorded run's provider as an explicit override, while a plain stage advance re-resolves the chain and uses the task's stamp only as the final fallback. Provider-specific model and effort values are layer-coherent: Kanna never combines them across providers or layers. It walks the same chain and takes the first value from a layer that would itself select the resolved provider. In an ordered provider list, model and effort belong only to the leading candidate; fallback candidates use a lower coherent layer or their own stamped/default values. `autocompact` follows the same coherence rule and is Claude-only.

model.description: Model id for the provider this entry selects — the first name in `provider`. It is not applied to any other provider, including a fallback candidate listed behind that name; such a candidate takes its model from a lower layer written for it, or runs on its own stamped or default model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for the provider this entry selects — the first name in `provider`. Effort vocabularies are provider-specific, so this value is not applied to any other provider; a fallback candidate listed behind that name takes its effort from a lower layer written for it, or runs on its own stamped or default effort.

autocompact.description: Claude only: the auto-compact window for the provider this entry selects — the first name in `provider`. `auto` (the model's native window) or 100k-1M tokens (`500k`, `200000`, `0.5M`, or `200` as shorthand for 200k). Kanna passes `auto` when nothing is configured, so a session never inherits the machine-wide `autoCompactWindow` from the operator's own `~/.claude/settings.json`. It is not applied to a fallback candidate listed behind that name, and naming it for a non-claude provider is an error.

artifacts.description: `artifacts` configures the repository's artifact store: a bare Git repository outside the working repository that holds published mockups, documents, media, and reports addressed by their Git tree id. `repositoryPath` defaults to `~/.kanna/repos/<repo-id>/artifacts.git`; a relative path resolves against the repository root, `~/` against the home directory, and any location inside the working repository, its Git directory, or one of its worktrees is refused. `retention` is `keep` (the default), `30-days`, or `discard-on-close`; it is recorded on each published version, and all content is currently retained regardless. `remote` names the artifact remote used to share artifacts with another Kanna home: an ordinary Git remote both can reach, as an absolute or `~/` path, a `file`, `ssh`, `git`, `http` or `https` URL, or scp-style `host:path`; remote helpers such as `ext::` are refused. Git's own SSH keys and credential helpers authenticate, and only artifact content with its version, comment and decision records is pushed there. Local config may set any of these fields, and a local field replaces only that field.

workspace.description: `ports` maps environment-variable names to base ports; Kanna reserves task-specific ports and exports the resolved values so parallel worktrees do not collide. `vars` provides committed string substitutions for agent prompts. `workspace`, `stage_order`, `reserved_ports`, and `reserved_port_offsets` are committed task semantics and cannot appear in local config.

model.description: Opaque native model ID. OpenCode uses backend/model; suffixes are literal.

effort.description: Exact native effort or variant; no compact aliases are expanded.

autocompact.description: Claude only: this session's auto-compact window — `auto` (the model's native window) or 100k-1M tokens (`500k`, `200000`, `0.5M`, or `200` as shorthand for 200k). Kanna passes `auto` when nothing is configured, so a session never inherits the machine-wide `autoCompactWindow` from the operator's own `~/.claude/settings.json`. Naming it beside any other harness is an error: no other CLI has the flag.
